question.text: Lotus Capital AIF's investee, Saraswati Infra Ltd, has a pre-tax cost of debt of 10%, cost of equity of 18%, debt-to-equity ratio 1:1, and a tax rate of 30%. Compute the WACC used for DCF valuation.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Post-tax cost of debt = 10% x (1 - 0.30) = 7%. With D/E = 1:1, weights are 50% debt and 50% equity. WACC = (0.50 x 7%) + (0.50 x 18%) = 3.5% + 9% = 12.5%. This matches the Box 11.1 methodology of the PDF for Cat I/II DCF valuation. **The Trap:** 14.00% ignores the tax shield (uses pre-tax kd); 11.00% uses wrong debt weight; 12.00% uses 20% tax instead of 30%. Always tax-adjust only the cost of debt (equity returns are not tax deductible to the firm). **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C (All-Cat Manager) covers identical WACC mechanics. XXI-B (Portfolio Manager) applies WACC mainly on listed equity where ke comes from pure CAPM; in AIF Cat I/II, ke carries an additional illiquidity premium. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** For unlisted PE targets, add a 3-5% illiquidity premium on top of CAPM-derived ke. Document the premium basis in your IC note — independent valuers will challenge an unadjusted ke for Cat II portfolio companies.
